reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes paid token packages with expected doubling within two to three months, multiple splits, and a very large one-year profit. The speaker also connects these return claims to team commissions and recruitment by directing viewers to join as a free rookie and bring in friends. Predictions about a future price rise and advice to use caution accompany, but do not remove, the package-return claims.

citations.quote: So if you can buy in and see what happens, click the link below.
For €140 you get a 1000 tokens, and then two to three months later you get 2000 tokens.
so basic whatever you do in two to three months you double your money.
If you buy two packs together, you can get four splits.
we're predicting, don't me on this, that the coin will double in price.

opening.argument: The presentation repeatedly qualifies its financial discussion instead of stating that returns are guaranteed. The speaker says the price increase is only a prediction, attributes a longer-term estimate to another person, and expressly tells viewers to invest only what they can afford. Those qualifications frame the figures as contingent scenarios and personal-risk guidance, not a promise of results. The invitation to investigate the opportunity should therefore be read alongside the explicit caution not to act imprudently.

citations.quote: we're predicting, don't me on this, that the coin will double in price
Dr. Ruja Ignatobos predicted that by the end of next year, it will be between 50 and 100
putting what you can afford to put in, don't become stupid

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited doubling language omits the speaker's qualification that it was a prediction and the accompanying warning about affordability. The package calculations are presented as conditional outcomes at different prices, while the speaker expressly says not to rely on the forecast as certainty. A cautious discussion of possible outcomes and risk is materially different from representing a return as assured.

citations.quote: we're predicting, don't me on this, that the coin will double in price
putting what you can afford to put in, don't become stupid

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Risk language does not neutralize the central sales message. The speaker still says that ordinary participation doubles money within two or three months and invites viewers to buy in. Calling a forecast a prediction merely softens one price claim; it does not explain away the asserted package-based return or the invitation to join.

citations.quote: so basic whatever you do in two to three months you double your money
So if you can buy in and see what happens, click the link below.

opening.argument: The video's evident format is an instructional walkthrough of a compensation spreadsheet. The speaker introduces herself as explaining how the system works and uses an Excel spreadsheet to work through token quantities, prices, splits, and hypothetical values. That is a demonstration of calculations and package mechanics, not proof that viewers were promised a particular outcome. The figures are shown as scenarios for understanding the model, and the incomplete audio itself makes the calculations unsuitable as a definitive offer.

citations.quote: i'm just going to explain to you, with my trusty Excel spreadsheet, how the actual system works when it comes to tokens
if it goes up from five point six five to ten .... then value after the split would be that
Now, put your maths test together

rebuttal.rebuttal: The spreadsheet format does not change what the lesson teaches. The walkthrough does more than explain arithmetic: it repeatedly calculates what viewers would receive after purchasing packages, recommends going as high as possible, and quantifies a projected profit. Calling those calculations educational leaves their persuasive purchase context unaddressed.

citations.quote: if at all possible, I would advise you to go as high as you can
it's 313,000 pound profit within a year

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The spreadsheet is being used to sell an opportunity, not merely to teach arithmetic. The speaker concludes that participants double their money, describes a huge profit within a year, and directs viewers to click a link. Those surrounding statements make the demonstration a promotional pitch regardless of its instructional presentation.

citations.quote: so basic whatever you do in two to three months you double your money
So if you can buy in and see what happens, click the link below.
it's 313,000 pound profit within a year

opening.argument: The material can be understood as ordinary commerce involving paid token packages and a referral opportunity, without evidence in the supplied record of credential collection, a guaranteed withdrawal, or a completed transaction. The speaker explains package prices and token quantities, while the spreadsheet displays package-value calculations. The referral language is also described as a commission arrangement, not as proof that every participant must recruit others. The record shows an offer and its proposed mechanics, but does not establish that the projected figures were achieved or independently verified.

citations.quote: this is the basic packages that you can buy in England
the other way of getting money is if you get people in your team

rebuttal.rebuttal: This is not ordinary retail merely because packages have prices. The speaker links purchasing to doubling money, multiple splits, team commissions, and a link to join. The absence of a credential request or completed withdrawal cannot establish legitimacy when the promotional mechanism itself is the subject of the video.

citations.quote: so basic whatever you do in two to three months you double your money
if I get Freddie who gets Jimmy I get ten percent of what ever they do

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing items are not decisive: scam promotion can occur before credentials or withdrawals are shown. Here, paid packages are tied to claimed rapid doubling, extra splits, and commissions from people in a team. The explicit invitation to buy in and become a rookie confirms that this is solicitation, not neutral retail description.
